neighbours.label: 'you' / 'ever' in an if-clause or relative clause just before a verb of wanting or planning (if you ever hope, the places you want); the output promotes plan/decide/want
fire: If you ever hope to buy a house, start saving now.
Pick the recipes you intend to cook this week.
If you are going to adopt a cat, prepare the house first.
Whatever you choose to wear, be comfortable.
If they ever want to return, the door is open.
List the places you would like to visit.
If you plan on hiking, bring water.
Any topic you wish to discuss is welcome.
quiet: You bought a house near the river last year.
The recipes were cooked by the chef this week.
Your cat sleeps on the windowsill every afternoon.
She wore a comfortable coat to the party.
They returned home late after the game.
We visited three museums during the trip.
Hiking in the hills was hot and tiring.
The topic was discussed at length in class.

notes: Probe: if-you-ever / relative 'you' ~0.2-0.25, main-clause You ~0.04. Borderline median.
